description_full: Azul S.A., together with its subsidiaries, provides air transportation services in Brazil and internationally. It is also involved in the cargo or postal; passenger charter; development of frequent-flyer programs; intellectual property owner; travel packages; funding: aircraft financing; and provision of maintenance and hangarage services for aircraft, engines, parts and pieces, aircraft acquisition, and lease services. As of December 31, 2025, the company operated approximately 970 daily departures to 160 destinations through a network of 390 non-stop routes; with an operating fleet of 176 aircraft and a passenger contractual fleet of 227 aircraft. The company was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in Barueri, Brazil.

financial_summary: Azul S.A. is a small-cap industrials business with a $874M market cap on $3.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.
The company is burning through $260M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.1× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
